answer: Each AI agent must bind its identity to a physically fused attestation key inside a hardware enclave; that key hashes to a vertex in a global graph and submits a fresh remote attestation every five minutes. The registry stores the key at that vertex and rejects any second attestation from the same key during an epoch, so a sybil attacker must buy one separate enclave processor per fake identity, about nine dollars each plus energy. Ten thousand fake agents cost about ninety thousand dollars in hardware, a pile of timber sunk into a karst sinkhole.
